subject: RFI: Support communications, TAM hours, and escalation timelines
messages:
From: Michael Allen <michael.allen@northshore.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwoodhq.com
Cc: procurement@northshore.com, emily.park@northshore.com
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Clarification on TAM coverage & incident comms

Alex —

Thanks for the RFI packet you sent last week. The procurement team and I are reviewing the support appendix and we have a few clarifying questions before we finalize our vendor shortlist. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm guaranteed TAM coverage windows (daytime vs overnight) and how handoffs are handled across timezones?
- For Sev1/Sev2 incidents, what are your on-call paging/acknowledgement SLAs and follow-up cadence to the customer?
- Do you provide a customer-facing incident timeline for every P1 and can that be pushed into our status page?

Appreciate a short response and any artifacts you can attach (on-call schedule sample, incident comm runbook). We have an internal deadline Friday EOD to pull together questions for your security/compliance team.

Best,
Michael Allen
Director of Infrastructure
Northshore Bank
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodhq.com>
To: Michael Allen <michael.allen@northshore.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodhq.com, ben.carter@redwoodhq.com
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM coverage & incident comms

Michael —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and I attached a concise RFI response PDF with examples. Longer notes follow.

- TAM coverage windows: Primary TAM coverage for enterprise contracts is 8am–8pm local business hours (customer primary region) with 24x7 on-call escalation to engineering for P1s. We maintain regional TAM pools in US/EU to minimize handoffs.
- Handoffs: Handoffs are documented in our on-call roster with explicit UTC windows and a handover checklist; we perform overlapping 1-hour shadow windows for cross-region transfers.
- P1/P2 SLAs: P1: initial paging & acknowledgement target 15 minutes; first status update to customer within 30 minutes; continuous updates every 60 minutes until mitigation. P2: acknowledgement target 1 hour; status update within 4 hours.
- Customer-facing timelines: Yes — for every P1 we publish an incident timeline (summary + timeline of key actions) within 24 hours, and a post-incident RCA within 5 business days (or a scheduled cadence agreed during SOW). We can publish to your status page via an API webhook or provide content you can paste.

Attachments included: redwood_support_rfi_response_v1.pdf (summary), sample oncall_rotations_utc_v2.csv (format), high-level incident-comm-runbook-abridged.md

Longer notes (quick bullets):
- Escalation path: TAM -> Escalation Engineer -> On-call Infra Eng -> Platform SRE Lead -> Customer Exec Alert (escalation matrix attached in PDF).
- Regional coverage: We staff TAMs in US/EU/APAC; enterprise customers can request dedicated TAM allocations and blackout windows.
- Pager noise & escalation discipline: We enforce a pager policy with automated dedupe for noisy alerts and a secondary channel for high-severity customer-impact signals.

I'll loop Marissa (CS Lead) and Ben (Support Ops) to confirm operational details and share the runbook link. If you want, we can set a 30-min call to walk through the sample runbook before Friday.

— Alex
Customer Solutions & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_support_rfi_response_v1.pdf (3 pages)
From: Emily Park <emily.park@northshore.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwoodhq.com
Cc: Michael Allen <michael.allen@northshore.com>, procurement@northshore.com
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM coverage & incident comms

Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick response. A couple follow-ups after reading the PDF:

1) Northshore runs critical services across US-East and APAC; we need to confirm overlap windows so the handoff doesn’t create blind hours. Can you share an example two-week rotation showing the UTC handoffs?
2) For the customer-facing incident timeline, is there a standard JSON payload you can emit (webhook) or do customers receive an email-formatted summary only? Our status page ingestion prefers structured data.
3) On acknowledgement targets: do you have a historical SLA adherence report (monthly) we can see for large customers?

Also procurement asked whether the TAM will be available for quarterly in-person reviews — is that included or an add-on?

Emily
Sr. Sourcing Manager
Northshore Bank
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodhq.com>
To: emily.park@northshore.com, michael.allen@northshore.com
Cc: alex.martinez@redwoodhq.com, ben.carter@redwoodhq.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodhq.com
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM coverage & incident comms

Emily / Michael —

Appreciate the questions. Quick clarifications from CS ops:

- I've attached a sanitized two-week rotation CSV (oncall_rotations_utc_v2.csv) that shows the UTC handoffs and overlapping shadow hours. In practice, we schedule a 1-hour overlap between region shifts (e.g., US shift 1500–0300 UTC overlaps APAC 2200–1000 UTC for handover).
- Incident timeline webhook: We publish a compact JSON schema for P1 timelines (fields: incident_id, start_time, severity, status_updates[] with timestamps + message). We can provide a DocuSign approval if Northshore needs the webhook contract language.
- SLA adherence reports: We provide monthly SLA adherence exports for enterprise customers as part of the Dedicated contract; we can share a redacted sample report for your review (slas-report-202606.csv).
- Quarterly in-person TAM reviews: available as an add-on in the enterprise package; two paid onsite days per quarter are typical, but we can include them in the SOW if you prefer.

Next step: Alex/Ben/Karthik and I will produce the sanitized rotations + a sample webhook payload and a one-page runbook tailored to your preferred escalation contacts. Can we target EOD Friday (2026-08-07) to deliver that bundle?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: oncall_rotations_utc_v2.csv (sample schedule)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodhq.com>
To: Michael Allen <michael.allen@northshore.com>, emily.park@northshore.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodhq.com, ben.carter@redwoodhq.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodhq.com
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM coverage & incident comms

Michael / Emily —

Deliverables attached per Marissa's note:
- incident-comm-runbook-20260807.md (one-page runbook + publish/playbook bullets)
- oncall_rotations_utc_v2.csv (two-week sample)
- redwood_support_rfi_response_v1.pdf (updated with webhook schema appendix)
- slas-report-202606-sample.csv (redacted SLA adherence sample)

Highlights:
- We will provide a webhook JSON schema for P1 timelines, sample payload included in the PDF appendix and as a Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-runbooks
- P1 acknowledgement target: 15 minutes (measured from first page). Historical adherence for similar enterprise customers for the trailing 6 months is 94.6% for P1 acknowledgements; full monthly exports are available under Dedicated contracts.
- Onsite TAM days: available as an add-on; we estimate travel + delivery costs will be included in the SOW line item if you choose quarterly on-site reviews.

If this bundle satisfies your team's needs we'll update the RFI response and add a short appendix to the commercial SOW. If you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough, I'm available Monday morning PST.

Thanks for the quick turn — looking forward to your sign-off.

— Alex
Customer Solutions & GTM
Redwood Inference
